root_cause.text: The boundary check in `iommu_mmio_write()` incorrectly validates the user-provided offset against a 4-byte access limit, whereas the corresponding read handler `iommu_mmio_show()` performs an 8-byte (64-bit) read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the boundary check in `drivers/iommu/amd/debugfs.c` being updated from `iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4` to `iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - sizeof(u64)`. The CVE description explains that `iommu_mmio_show()` uses `readq()` to perform an 8-byte read, which causes a 4-byte out-of-bounds read if the offset is set to `mmio_phys_end - 4`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the vulnerability. In `iommu_mmio_write()`, the user-supplied offset is validated against a 4-byte limit: `iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4`. However, the corresponding read handler `iommu_mmio_show()` performs an 8-byte read using `readq(iommu->mmio_base + iommu->dbg_mmio_offset)`. This mismatch allows reading up to 4 bytes past the end of the MMIO region.
